q: How do I calculate Scope 3 waste emissions for a chemical plant from hazardous waste manifests and TSDF invoices in India?
title: Hazardous waste emissions from manifests
short: Group the tonnes on your manifests and TSDF invoices by waste type and treatment route (secured landfill, incineration, co-processing, recycling), then multiply each group by a factor for that route. Incineration of solvent or organic waste usually dominates; calculate it from the waste's fossil carbon content. Report the total as Scope 3 Category 5.
audience: Chemical and pharma units in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Telangana

ul: The manifest under the Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules, 2016 (Form 10) travels with each consignment and records the waste category, quantity and the receiving facility.
The TSDF or recycler invoice gives the billed tonnes and usually names the service: landfill, incineration or co-processing. This is the cleanest activity data.
Your annual return to the state pollution control board totals the year by category, and is a good cross-check.
A waste analysis or acceptance report from the TSDF gives calorific value or carbon content, needed for incineration.

Incineration: CO2 = tonnes x carbon content (fraction of wet weight) x fossil share of that carbon x oxidation factor x 44/12. Use the TSDF's analysis for carbon content; IPCC 2006 Volume 5, Chapter 5 gives the method and default oxidation.
Secured landfill: tonnes x a landfill factor for the waste type. Mostly inorganic hazardous waste produces little methane; organic sludge produces more.

Co-processing in cement kilns and recycling: the guidance generally assigns combustion or recycling emissions to the user of the recovered energy or material. Report transport, or a sourced route factor, and state the approach you took.
Waste transport to the TSDF may be included in Category 5; say whether you did.

p: There is no official Indian factor set for hazardous waste treatment. Options, in order of preference: data from your TSDF, calculation from the waste's own composition, or a published route factor such as the UK DESNZ waste disposal tables, labelled as a non-Indian proxy. Write the source and year with every factor.

ul: Using the rupee amount on the invoice as activity data. TSDF rates vary with waste type and distance, not emissions.
Counting a consignment twice, once from the manifest and again from the invoice. Pick one as the record and reconcile tonnes.
Treating ETP sludge and spent solvent with one factor. Their carbon content differs widely.
Leaving out wastewater sent off site, which also belongs in Category 5.

example.title: Worked example: spent solvent sent for incineration
lines: TSDF invoice: 20 t of spent solvent waste, route: incineration
TSDF analysis: carbon content 60% of wet weight (assumed for this example), all fossil
example.note: The carbon content is an assumption for illustration. Use your TSDF's waste analysis, and remember that waste with biogenic carbon has a lower fossil share.

senseible: Senseible keeps TSDF and waste service invoice lines in a separate Scope 3 evidence trail with the source page and the file's SHA-256 fingerprint. A line gets a figure only when its printed quantity, unit and treatment route match an approved factor; otherwise it shows Needs Data, with no spend-based fill. It does not read manifests or calculate incineration from waste composition.
